Cookies for the key cabinet inside the VPN connection

cabinet.dataNote: We do not need this data ourselves, but it is the minimum set required by law for requests from authorities in VPN server jurisdictions. All data is encrypted with a key split across the team per day and per squad so the key can only be decrypted with majority consent of key holders, and only what is requested will be decrypted.

faq.question: How do I see how much traffic I have left?
answers: The remainder is shown on your user card (the first card in the list)

faq.question: How can a user know how much traffic they have left?
answers: They ask you, and you check their card

faq.question: Which country is my server in?
answers: Definitely outside Russia/Belarus, in a country with rule of law. We know exactly where yours is, but we will not tell you :)

faq.question: How much traffic do I get in total?
answers: Each user gets 100 GB. Limits reset at the start of each month.
If you are SUPER-VIP with an unlimited key — full freedom, no caps.

faq.question: How many devices can connect to one key cabinet?
answers: One key cabinet can hold up to 250 configs at once. If you are nearing the limit, remove inactive users (see statuses “dead soul” and “hedgehog in the fog”).

faq.question: Can I choose the country I connect to?
answers: Not in the current version. Our focus is your safety; we rotate IPs regularly.

faq.question: What if someone gets my name and six words or my file — what happens to me, my squad, and you?
answers: If a stranger gets your login and six words, they can reissue the brigadier config. The old one is disabled immediately and you lose the squad.
Users you added may be deleted. IPs could theoretically be enriched via providers, but outsiders still cannot see traffic.

faq.question: What if I forgot/lost the six magic words and/or brigadier name? What happens to my users?
answers: If you are reading this here, your username is on the first card.
No one can restore the six words — not even with a puppy held hostage.
You can manage the squad until you lose the config file. Support can use the brigadier name.
If the file is gone, the squad is on its own; you cannot help those you shared configs with.
We suggest reissuing the squad and redistributing keys — your choice :)

i1.q: How is Pro Basic different from Pro Unlim?
i1.a: Pro Basic works with the base speed and traffic limits, like regular keys. Pro Unlim has no traffic limits and comes with extended quotas. In both cases you set the validity term yourself.

i2.a: Nothing. They work as before, indefinitely, and never enter the invoice. PRO does not auto-delete Free keys.

i3.a: Once a month, on the 1st, for all paid keys at once. If a key was created mid-month, the first time you only pay for the days it actually worked.

i4.q: What if I don't pay on time?
i4.a: There is a week of grace. After that paid keys are switched off but not deleted. Names and comments are kept. After payment the keys become active again. Free keys keep working.

i5.q: How is switching a key off different from deleting it?
i5.a: A switched-off key is kept and can become active again. A deleted key cannot be restored - a new one has to be created instead.

i6.q: Can a Free key be moved to Pro?
i6.a: Yes, with the “Upgrade” button on the card. The key is reissued, so it has to be added to the VPN client again. The old key keeps working for 3 more days and then switches off.

i7.a: Better to have access to all three - VLESS, Outline and Gate 19. Under blocking they may behave differently: one protocol may stop connecting while another keeps working. Each comes with a link and an access key; you can switch between them on the key card.

i8.a: Only you. The comment is not shown in the list - a small mark appears next to the name. Do not put names, surnames or other personal data in comments.

i9.q: What does the person I sent a key to see?
i9.a: Only the data needed to connect the VPN. Comments and internal brigade information are not shown to them.

s1.label: step 1 of 7
s1.title: PRO is on - the shortage is cancelled
s1.text: No move was needed: same keys, same list, same buttons. It's just that next to the free ones you can now get paid ones - no queue and no connections required.

s2.label: step 2 of 7 · key labels
s2.title: Keys got labels
s2.text: Every key now carries a label. Issued for free - you get Free. Issued for sale - Pro Basic or Pro Unlim. The label is visible right in the list. And the brigade won't be quietly written off anymore - deletion protection is part of PRO too.

cards.name: Pro Basic
cards.body: you set the term, goes into the common invoice

s3.label: step 3 of 7 · the table
s3.title: Keys can be viewed as a table
s3.text: Next to the “+ New key” button there is a “Table” switch. One click - all keys, labels, traffic and status in rows, no card scrolling.

s4.label: step 4 of 7 · how to issue a paid key
s4.title: Two roads to Pro
s4.text: The first - the red “+ New key” button in the top right: pick a plan, a term, sign and pay. The second - the “Upgrade” link right on a free key's card: the key is reissued, so it has to be added to the VPN client again - the old key works 3 more days and quietly retires.

s5.label: step 5 of 7 · invoices
s5.title: Invoices arrived!
s5.text: Payment was never a thing before - now paid keys come with an invoice: one common bill for all paid keys at once, no separate bill per key.

cards.name: One bill
cards.body: All paid keys in one bill, paid once a month.

cards.name: A key mid-month
cards.body: The first payment covers only the remaining days, not the whole month.

cards.name: Overdue
cards.body: Then paid keys are switched off temporarily; Free keys keep working.

s6.label: step 6 of 7 · analytics
s6.title: Analytics added
s6.text: The top menu got an “Analytics” section: revenue, MRR, inactive users and hints on what to do next. Have a look - it's not just numbers, it's ready-made recommendations.

s7.label: step 7 of 7
s7.title: Welcome to a world with no shortage
s7.text: The guide can always be reopened - “How PRO works” in the top menu. Happy selling!
